## Welcome to the NSIDC Data Cookbook! 

This Cookbook for National Snow and Ice Data Center Distributed Active Archive Center ([NSIDC DAAC](https://nsidc.org/data/data-programs/nsidc-daac)) data is intended to be more like Julia Child's Mastering the Art of French Cooking than a simple collection of recipes (or data tutorials). Our goal is not only to provide easy-to-follow recipes for working with data, but also to build an understanding of the data managed by NSIDC and the tools available to work with it.

Rather than providing an in-depth guide to every dataset housed at NSIDC, this cookbook introduces common data types, file formats, and data structures. We hope it will provide the guidance and foundation you need to *master the art of working with cryospheric data*.

## How to use this cookbook

If you are new to NASA or NSIDC data, begin with the **Getting Started** section. Beyond that, the cookbook is divided into three major sections: **NSIDC Data**, **Working with Data**, and **Tutorials / Workshops**. We also include **Appendices** that include a list of video learning resources, a glossary, and how to contribute to the cookbook (if you are so inclined!).

The **NSIDC Data** section introduces the types of data managed by NSIDC, the file formats used to store that data, coordinate reference systems and grids commmonly used with NSIDC data, and NASA terminology for Earth science data. 

The **Working with Data** section provides guidance on tools, applications, and workflows for accomplishing common tasks when working with NSIDC data. It is organized into three subsections:

- *Finding and Accessing Data:* How-to guides for discovering and accessing NSIDC data.

- *Wrangling Data:* How-to guides for manipulating data, including subsetting, reformatting, reprojecting, and resampling in preparation for analysis.

- *Visualizing Data:* How-to guides for creating plots and visualizing data.

The **Tutorials / Workshops** section provides step-by-step workflows for working with NSIDC data. These tutorials are designed to be self-contained and can serve as starting points for your own analyses. Some tutorials were developed for specific workshops and are preserved in their original form for past participants to reference, while others are designed for self-paced learning and are updated over time.

## About the NSIDC DAAC

NSIDC has managed the NASA National Snow and Ice Data Center Distributed Active Archive Center (NSIDC DAAC) since 1993, archiving and distributing cryospheric and related geophysical data from NASA Earth-observing satellite missions, airborne campaigns and field observations. The NSIDC DAAC provides hundreds of free and open-access NASA Earth science data sets, detailed data documentation, data tools, resources and tutorials, as well as  robust data user support services. These data support research on topics relating to snow cover, sea ice, ice sheets, ice shelves, glaciers, frozen ground, soil moisture, climate interactions, and more!
